title: WorkSquare
headline: WorkSquare, a community-driven career platform
summary: I founded WorkSquare, a bootstrapped Indian career platform that brings job search, skill-based communities, and free voice AI interview prep into one product.

sections.title: Overview
body: WorkSquare is the career platform I founded and still build. It is made for people who want more than a static job board: a public feed of roles, communities around the work they want, a karma system that makes reputation visible, and recruiter tools in the same product.
The public site is at worksquare.co. The Android app, WorkSquare: Jobs & Careers, is on Google Play.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Job search is usually split across job boards, message threads, and interview prep tools that do not talk to each other. Hiring teams post in one place and review people in another. WorkSquare puts discovery, conversation, reputation, and applications on one platform.

sections.title: What it does
items: Browse and search open roles by job title, skill, company, location, and remote-work preference, with AI job matching in the product.
A public job and discussion feed where people can talk through roles, follow companies, and share hiring notes.
Skill-based career communities, plus karma and reputation that rise with useful comments and trusted activity.
Save roles, apply when ready, and message hiring teams directly.
Free voice-based AI interview prep, so you can practice before you talk to a hiring team.
Recruiter tools in the same product: create a company, post a job, review applications, and message candidates.

sections.title: Tech stack
sections.body: The web app is Next.js, running on Vercel, with Supabase for the backend and data. The Android app is a Capacitor wrapper around that product.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I founded WorkSquare and I own the product and the engineering.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: WorkSquare is live on the web at worksquare.co. The Android app went live on Google Play on 15 October 2026.

title: TradeFlock
headline: TradeFlock USA, a US business news site
summary: I own the engineering for TradeFlock USA, a US business news site covering markets, technology, finance, and leadership. I work there as an employee. I am not the owner or founder.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: TradeFlock USA publishes US business news at tradeflock.net. The desk covers markets, technology, finance, and leadership, in the tradition of a national business paper. I work on TradeFlock as an employee, and I own the engineering.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: A newsroom at this scale has to move wires into publishable stories every day, keep editors in control of what goes live, and still serve a large, frequently updated site without rebuilding every page by hand.

sections.title: What it does
items: A public news site with sections including Tech, Markets, Leadership, Finance, Success Insights, and a magazine.
An AI-assisted newsroom with desk bots that help the operation move work through the desks.
A wire editor publish gate, so stories do not go live until they pass editorial control.
Daily-cached pages, so the public site stays fast while the desk keeps publishing.
A dynamic sitemap. It currently lists about 2,000 URLs.

sections.title: Tech stack
sections.body: I built the site in Next.js, host it on Vercel, and use Supabase for the data layer. The public pages are cached daily.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I work at TradeFlock USA as an employee. I own the engineering for the site and the newsroom tools. I am not the owner or founder of TradeFlock.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: The site is live at tradeflock.net. The sitemap currently lists about 2,000 URLs, and the main section pages refresh daily.

title: People of LA
headline: People of LA, a walkable 3D city
summary: People of LA is a stylised 3D Los Angeles you can walk through in the browser, and meet fictional residents across Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, and Downtown.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: People of LA is a browser experience: a stylised 3D Los Angeles you can walk through, and a set of fictional residents placed across the city. It is live at peopleofla.online.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Most city sites describe a place with articles and photographs. I wanted a site you could actually walk, and where the people of the city were part of the map, not a separate directory.

sections.title: What it does
items: A walkable 3D Los Angeles in the browser, built on a WebGL city client.
Fictional residents you can meet across Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, and Downtown.
A membership layer: applications go under review, and approved members come from a Supabase project.

sections.title: Tech stack
sections.body: The city client is WebGL. A Node.js server serves the site and the membership API. Membership and approvals use Supabase. The live site is hosted on Vercel.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I built and shipped People of LA, including the city pack, the membership flow, and the live site.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: The site is live at peopleofla.online.

title: Documento
headline: Documento, an all-in-one document editor
summary: Documento is an offline Android document editor I built at Shivank Tech. It opens and edits Word, Excel, PDF, TXT, Markdown and image files right on your phone, with no account and no cloud, so confidential files never leave the device.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Documento is a private, offline workspace for documents, PDFs, notes, and everyday tasks. I built it at Shivank Tech as an Android app. There is no account and no cloud dependency. Your files stay on the device.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: A lot of document work still means uploading files to someone else's servers. That is a bad fit for confidential paperwork. Documento keeps the work on the phone, so you can edit, scan, and organize without a cloud account.

sections.title: What it does
items: Open and edit Word, Excel, PDF, TXT, Markdown, and image files on the phone. It does not include PowerPoint.

PDF tools: read and view, create PDFs from images and text, edit text and pictures, comments, highlights and drawings, fill and sign, merge files, rearrange and crop pages, compress, password-protect, export, and read documents aloud.
Scan paper documents with the camera and convert photos into PDFs, then work with the scans on the device.
Notes with text and images, to-do lists you can check off, and voice notes you record and play back in the same workspace.
Browse the workspace by All, Notes, To-Do, and PDFs, and jump back to recent files.

sections.title: Tech stack
sections.body: Documento is a native Android app from Shivank Tech. It is designed to work completely offline, with no account and no cloud.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I built Documento at Shivank Tech.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: Documento is live on Google Play.

title: Canvas
headline: Canvas, a photo and video editing hub
summary: Canvas is a mobile photo and video editing hub I built at Shivank Tech. It is a dedicated editor, with quick tools, templates, and video actions, rather than a filter bolted onto a feed.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Canvas is an Android photo and video editor from Shivank Tech. You can use the core editing features without creating an account. Photos and videos you select stay yours. The app processes them so you can adjust, retouch, apply presets, crop, transform, and export.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: A lot of mobile editing is buried inside a social feed. Canvas is a dedicated hub for people who want to edit photos and videos as their own work, with tools and templates in one place.

sections.title: What it does
items: Quick editing tools for everyday photo work, including retouch, presets, and related adjustments.
Photo templates, including featured looks such as Soft Light, Noir, and Golden Hour, plus create options for photos, video, presets, and retouch.
Video quick actions, including trim, resize, and text, with featured video templates such as Reel, Title, and Countdown.
A curated templates library, so you can start from a designed look instead of a blank canvas.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I built Canvas at Shivank Tech.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: Canvas is an Android app from Shivank Tech. Core editing does not require an account.

title: Booking systems
headline: Custom booking systems, built to each client's needs
summary: Through Shivank Tech, I build custom booking systems for local appointment businesses, fitted to how each client actually takes work: dentists, salons and spas, plumbers, and similar shops.

sections.title: Overview
body: Shivank Tech is my web and app studio. A large part of that work is custom booking systems for local businesses that run on appointments.
I do not ship one generic scheduler and hope it fits. Each system is built around that client's needs: who they serve, how they take bookings, and what has to happen after a slot is taken.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Dentists, clinics, salons, spas, plumbers, and other trades live and die by the next appointment. When booking is buried in a phone call or a generic form, they miss work, double-book, and spend the day chasing confirmations instead of doing the job. A generic scheduler can get a client part of the way there, but it rarely matches how that shop actually runs staff, rooms, payments, and follow-up.

sections.title: What it does
sections.body: I design and build the booking product around the business in front of me. The exact shape changes with the client. Typical systems I build include:
items: A salon or clinic appointment calendar, with staff in columns and time slots down the day, so the front desk can see who is free and avoid double-booking.
A customer-facing slot picker and checkout, so a client can choose a service, pick an open time, and confirm or pay without a phone call.
An admin dashboard for the day: today's bookings, who has arrived, no-shows, and what has been collected, with the work that still needs attention.
A client CRM: a searchable list of people, each with a profile and a history of visits, so the business can pick up where the last appointment left off.
Resource, room, or table booking, when the constraint is a space rather than a person: a treatment room, a private dining room, or a floor of tables.
Payments and invoices, plus reminder settings so the business can send visit reminders over WhatsApp or SMS, and follow up after a missed visit.

sections.title: Tech stack
sections.body: I build these systems with Next.js, Supabase, and Vercel. Payments go through a payment gateway, and reminders go out through WhatsApp or SMS integrations, wired to the client's own booking rules rather than a one-size-fits-all stack.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I lead this work at Shivank Tech: understand the client's booking problem, then design and build a system that matches it, from the public booking flow to the desk tools they use every day.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: This is ongoing product work at Shivank Tech for local appointment businesses. Each system is a separate build, shaped to that client, and stays with them as their booking tool.
